sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 16701 of 2025
Applicant :- Mohd. Amir

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Kr. Singh Paliwal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha,J.
1.

Heard Sri Santosh Kr. Singh Paliwal, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A for the
State.

2.  The present application has been filed for the following relief:
"To quash the charge sheet dated 18.07.2014 as well as summoning order dated 25.11.2016 and N.B.W order dated 18.01.2019 passed by member Magistrate,
Juvenile Justice Board, Aligarh as well as entire criminal proceeding of Case No.
183/2016 (State Vs. Amir), arising out of Case Crime No. 663 of 2012, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B I.P.C., Police Station Civil Lines, District Aligarh."
3.Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is juvenile and student of B.Tech and impugned order has been passed by the court without satisfying itself that the summon and other process for attendance has been served and without issuing any summon or bailable warrant, direct N.B.W. has been issued.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the impugned order has been passed without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and law provided in this regard.

It is further submitted that order of the non-bailable warrant has been passed on18.01.2019 without satisfying the service of summons or bailable warrants itself and reason to believe from absconding the process of the court.
5. Learned A.G.A. submits that the applicant has not been appearing before the Juvenile Justice Board for a long time.

6. On perusal of the certified copy of the order sheet commencing from 25.11.2016, it appears that there is no mention of service of summon on the applicant by learned Juvenile Justice Board,
Aligarh without recording any satisfaction regarding service of summon on the applicant, the Juvenile Justice Board, Aligarh proceeded to issue non bailable warrant against the applicant, which is against the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Indra Mohan Goswami Vs.
State of Uttrakhand, AIR 2008 Supreme Court 251 and Raghuvansh Diwan Chand Vs. N.C.T, Delhi,
AIR 2011 Supreme Court 3393.
7.Considering submissions of learned counsel for the applicant and perusing record, the present application is finally disposed of with a direction that in case applicant appears before the Juvenile Justice Board, Aligarh within three weeks from today and applies for bail/recall of non bailable warrant, his application shall be decided expeditiously, strictly in accordance with law.
8.
